comparativeConvention.method: Each landed repair was compared against frozen peer leftover-joins that carry the same leaf shapes and were themselves accepted, to establish that the repairs follow the lineage's convention rather than merely satisfying the literal text of the findings.
comparativeConvention.lastHeadingUniformity: Accepted peers hold last-heading custody uniformly at a single decision equal to their own last heading at dispatch: g20 leftover-join.v16 13x D-329, g20 leftover-join.v11 10x D-327, sdk leftover-join.v9 5x D-328. The subject now matches with 9x D-331 and zero competing values, and like g20 leftover-join.v16's d322 leaf it applies the rule even to the leaf whose own subject is a superseded last heading: basedOn.d321.role reads 'Historical last-heading of g19 leftover-join.v6. ... Last-heading custody remains D-331. Not last-heading of g19 leftover-join.v8.'
comparativeConvention.supersededPredecessorMarking: g20 leftover-join.v16 marks superseded predecessors with the bare form 'Historical after D-323.' / 'Historical after D-329.' The subject's repaired predecessorV5 leaf uses that form and then adds the explicit redirect to the standing recording, which is the stronger of the two conventions.
comparativeConvention.rejectedPredecessorLeaf: g20 leftover-join.v16 and sdk leftover-join.v9 both carry 'Findings land at <successor speaker>.' on the frozen rejected predecessor leaf. The subject's predecessorV7 leaf matches, naming v8.
comparativeConvention.pathShorthand: The subject writes 'fixtures/g19.v1/' and 'fixtures/g19.v2/' where the files live at docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g19.v*/. This is not charged: the shorthand is the settled lineage convention, appearing in dual-ACCEPT-0/0 g19 leftover-join.v6 and in dual-ACCEPT-0/0 g19-fixture-corpus.v3 itself, which uses the same shorthand alongside its 146 fully-qualified path citations. The corpus artifact, not the join, is the authority that enumerates the paths, and it enumerates them in full.

whatWouldHaveMadeThisReject: Any of: a surviving 'Last-heading custody remains D-321' leaf; a second present-tense currency claim competing with v6; obligations[4].reason still placing the forty-eight copies in leftover-design; leftoverDesign no longer the singleton [OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING]; an invented CODEX-* identifier; a fabricated D-002 platform list diverging from occupancy v2's four platforms; any SATISFIES claim against DR-124, DR-G19 or DR-117; a deictic speaker; or any one of the 91 cited digests failing to match live bytes. Each was tested and none occurred.
residualObservationsNotCharged: findingDisposition.codexV7MustFixLastHeading says 'Seven basedOn roles read Last-heading custody remains D-331' while nine basedOn roles in fact carry that sentence. Not charged at either grade: the sentence dispositions the seven locations Codex charged, both extras (d321, d322) already read D-331 in frozen v7 and were never part of the finding, and every one of the nine defers to the same heading, so no reader is routed to a competing custody value. The claim is exact as a repair-landing statement and creates no contradiction on the bytes.

basedOn carries fifteen historical leaves beyond those the findings touched. All were digest-checked and commit-resolved; none asserts a live currency, custody or closure claim that the subject contradicts elsewhere.
